A BRIEF TORNADO MOVED THROUGH CROPLAND JUST NORTH OF THE EASTERN IOWA AIRPORT. THE PATH WAS FOUND IN HIGH RESOLUTION SATELLITE IMAGERY. THE TORNADO WAS ON THE LEADING EDGE OF A LARGER SWATH OF STRAIGHT LINE WINDS THAT SNAPPED TREES AND DESTROYED OUTBUILDINGS AND GRAIN BINS. THE TORNADO WAS ON THE GROUND FOR ABOUT ONE MINUTE, TRAVELED JUST UNDER ONE MILE, AND HAD A MAXIMUM WIDTH OF ABOUT 40 YARDS. THERE WAS NO DAMAGE DIRECTLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE TORNADO FROM WHICH AN EF-SCALE RATING COULD BE ASSIGNED. THUS, THE TORNADO IS DESIGNATED EF-U.

A TORNADO MOVED THROUGH CROPLAND JUST SOUTH OF FREEPORT. THE TORNADO BEGAN JUST WEST OF FLORENCE, AND MOVED N/NE FOR ABOUT 4.5 MILES BEFORE DISSIPATING AT THE SOUTHERN EDGE OF FREEPORT. THE PATH WAS FOUND IN HIGH RESOLUTION SATELLITE IMAGERY AND CONFIRMED BY UAS SURVEY. THE TORNADO WAS ON THE GROUND FOR ABOUT 5 MINUTES AND THE MAXIMUM WIDTH WAS AROUND 50 YARDS. THE TORNADO WAS ON THE LEADING EDGE OF A LARGER SWATH OF DAMAGING STRAIGHT LINE WINDS. THERE WAS NO DAMAGE DIRECTLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE TORNADO FROM WHICH AN EF-SCALE RATING COULD BE ASSIGNED. THUS, THE TORNADO IS DESIGNATED EF-U.

A BRIEF EF-1 TORNADO WITH PEAK WINDS OF 100 MPH, PATH LENGTH OF 0.75 MILES, AND MAX WIDTH OF 150 YARDS IMPACTED THE NORTH SIDE OF OTTAWA DAMAGING ROOFING MATERIAL AND SHREDDING TREES ALONG ITS PATH. THE ROOFING MATERIAL WAS ORIGINALLY WELL-ANCHORED TO THE WALLS, AND A NEARBY SNAPPED POWER POLE SUGGESTED A PEAK INTENSITY OF 100 MPH WINDS. EYE WITNESS ACCOUNTS CONFIRM THE DAMAGE WAS PRODUCED BY A TORNADO BASED ON CLEARLY RISING AND SWIRLING MOTION BY MULTIPLE SUB-VORTICES IN A BROAD CIRCULATION.

AN EF-1 TORNADO WITH PEAK WINDS OF 95 MPH AND PATH LENGTH OF 5.7 MILES TOUCHED DOWN ON HARMONY ROAD SOUTHWEST OF I-90 AND CONTINUED NORTHEAST BEFORE LIFTING NEAR DUNHAM ROAD BETWEEN MARENGO AND UNION. MOST DAMAGE WAS CONFINED TO TREES AND TO FARM BUILDINGS ALONG THE PATH.

AN EF-1 TORNADO WITH PEAK WINDS OF 105 MPH, PATH LENGTH OF 14.5 MILES, AND MAX WIDTH OF 250 YARDS STARTED ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF YORKVILLE DESTROYING A PERGOLA, TAKING SIDING OFF A HOUSE, AND THROWING A TREE ACROSS A ROAD. THE TORNADO THEN CONTINUED SOUTHEAST AND DAMAGED SEVERAL FARMSTEADS INCLUDING THROWING A SHED SEVERAL HUNDRED FEET INTO A FIELD AND SCOURING GRASS. SEVERAL POWER POLES WERE SNAPPED AT THEIR BASE, AS WELL. THE TORNADO CROSSED INTO WILL COUNTY SOUTH OF PLAINFIELD AND CONTINUED DAMAGING TREES UNTIL ENDING JUST WEST OF I-55 NEAR CANTON FARM ROAD. A BROAD AREA OF WIND GUSTS OF 70 TO 80 MPH THEN FOLLOWED INTO CREST HILL LEADING TO PROLIFIC TREE DAMAGE.
